title: AXI4 Memory-Mapped Signal Quick Reference
description: Expand a signal to review its owner, accepting edge, encoding or role, and the monitor mistake most likely to corrupt transaction reconstruction.

signals.name: ACLK
signals.description: All AXI transfers are recognized on the rising edge of ACLK.
signals.verificationNote: Sample every channel in one clocking discipline and account explicitly for any clock-domain bridge.

signals.name: ARESETn
signals.description: Reset can assert asynchronously but deasserts synchronously with a rising ACLK edge.
signals.verificationNote: During reset, a manager drives AWVALID, WVALID, and ARVALID LOW; prevent the monitor from creating phantom transactions at release.

signals.name: AWID
signals.description: Selects the write response-ordering stream and is reflected on BID.
signals.verificationNote: Allocate a queue entry per accepted AW; one slot per numeric ID is insufficient.

signals.name: AWADDR
signals.description: Address of the first byte transfer in the write burst.
values: May be unaligned for supported INCR transfers
signals.verificationNote: Keep the accepted address with AWLEN/AWSIZE/AWBURST; later W beats carry no address.

signals.name: AWLEN
signals.description: AWLEN+1 is the exact number of W transfers in the burst.
signals.verificationNote: Count accepted W beats only and require WLAST on the declared final transfer.

signals.name: AWSIZE
signals.description: Each W transfer covers up to 2^AWSIZE bytes, subject to bus width and byte strobes.
signals.verificationNote: Reject sizes wider than the interface and derive byte lanes together with AWADDR and WSTRB.

signals.name: AWBURST
signals.description: Selects FIXED, INCR, or WRAP address generation for the write burst.
signals.verificationNote: Check WRAP length/alignment and that the complete burst remains inside one 4 KB region.

signals.name: AWLOCK
signals.description: In AXI4, indicates a normal or exclusive write request.
signals.verificationNote: Match an exclusive write to its completed exclusive read and check all exclusive span and attribute restrictions.

signals.name: AWCACHE
signals.description: Defines Bufferable, Modifiable, Read-allocate, and Write-allocate transaction attributes in AXI4.
signals.verificationNote: Do not decode bit 1 as the AXI3 Cacheable meaning; AXI4 names it Modifiable.

signals.name: AWPROT
signals.description: Carries privileged/unprivileged, secure/non-secure, and instruction/data attributes.
signals.verificationNote: Check system permission policy separately from the protocol encoding.

signals.name: AWQOS
signals.description: A 4-bit identifier available to an implementation-defined system QoS policy.
values: Higher value recommended as higher priority
signals.verificationNote: AXI does not mandate one arbitration algorithm or starvation bound; verify the documented system policy.

signals.name: AWREGION
signals.description: Distinguishes up to 16 logical regions that can share an address range.
signals.verificationNote: Do not treat AWREGION as extra address bits; its interpretation is system-specific.

signals.name: AWUSER
signals.description: Optional application-defined information carried with the AW payload.
signals.verificationNote: If implemented, include AWUSER in stalled-payload stability and end-to-end route checks.

signals.name: AWVALID
signals.description: Asserted by the manager when the complete AW payload is valid.
signals.verificationNote: Must not depend on AWREADY and must remain asserted with stable payload until acceptance.

signals.name: AWREADY
signals.description: Asserted by the subordinate when it can accept the AW payload.
signals.verificationNote: READY may wait for VALID, but the interface must not create a combinational input-to-output path.

signals.name: WDATA
signals.description: Carries one write-data transfer; AXI4 associates W bursts with AW requests in address order.
signals.verificationNote: AXI4 has no WID. Preserve accepted AW order while allowing W to arrive before its AW handshake.

signals.name: WSTRB
signals.description: One bit per WDATA byte lane indicates which bytes carry valid write data.
signals.verificationNote: Check strobes against address, transfer size, and supported unaligned behavior; hold them stable during stalls.

signals.name: WLAST
signals.description: Asserted with the final W transfer declared by AWLEN.
signals.verificationNote: Flag both early assertion and absence on the final accepted beat; AXI does not support early burst termination.

signals.name: WUSER
signals.description: Optional application-defined information carried per W transfer.
signals.verificationNote: Include WUSER in stability and data-route checking when present.

signals.name: WVALID
signals.description: Asserted by the manager when WDATA, WSTRB, WLAST, and optional WUSER are valid.
signals.verificationNote: Must not wait for WREADY and can assert before AW is accepted.

signals.name: WREADY
signals.description: Asserted by the subordinate when it can accept a W transfer.
signals.verificationNote: Randomize independently from AWREADY and BREADY to expose channel-skew FIFO boundaries.

signals.name: BID
signals.description: Identifies the accepted AW transaction receiving this write response.
signals.verificationNote: Match the head outstanding entry for BID and preserve response issue order for repeated IDs.

signals.name: BRESP
signals.description: One response qualifies the complete write burst.
signals.verificationNote: EXOKAY is only an exclusive success; an unsuccessful exclusive write returns OKAY without updating the location.

signals.name: BUSER
signals.description: Optional application-defined information returned with BRESP.
signals.verificationNote: Include BUSER in stable-payload and route/correlation checks when present.

signals.name: BVALID
signals.description: Asserted when BID, BRESP, and optional BUSER form a valid response.
signals.verificationNote: For AXI4, do not assert before an AW handshake and the accepted WLAST transfer; never wait for BREADY before asserting.

signals.name: BREADY
signals.description: Asserted by the manager when it can accept a write response.
signals.verificationNote: Backpressure must not cause BID, BRESP, BUSER, or BVALID to change.

signals.name: ARID
signals.description: Selects the read response-ordering stream and is reflected on every RID beat.
signals.verificationNote: Allocate a FIFO entry within ARID so repeated-ID reads retire in request order.

signals.name: ARADDR
signals.description: Address of the first byte transfer in the read burst.
values: May be unaligned for supported INCR transfers
signals.verificationNote: Predict all later byte addresses and lanes because the R channel carries no address.

signals.name: ARLEN
signals.description: ARLEN+1 is the exact number of R transfers in the burst.
signals.verificationNote: Count accepted R beats and require RLAST on the declared final beat even after an error response.

signals.name: ARSIZE
signals.description: Each R transfer covers up to 2^ARSIZE bytes, subject to interface width.
signals.verificationNote: Use ARADDR and ARSIZE to select the meaningful RDATA byte lanes.

signals.name: ARBURST
signals.description: Selects FIXED, INCR, or WRAP address generation for the read burst.
signals.verificationNote: Check generated addresses, legal WRAP configuration, and the complete 4 KB span.

signals.name: ARLOCK
signals.description: In AXI4, indicates a normal or exclusive read request.
signals.verificationNote: An EXOKAY read records monitor state; an OKAY response means failed or unsupported exclusive handling.

signals.name: ARCACHE
signals.description: Defines Bufferable, Modifiable, Read-allocate, and Write-allocate attributes in AXI4.
signals.verificationNote: Verify downstream transformations preserve the permitted visibility and ordering behavior.

signals.name: ARPROT
signals.description: Carries privileged/unprivileged, secure/non-secure, and instruction/data attributes.
signals.verificationNote: Check denied accesses and returned DECERR/SLVERR behavior against the system security architecture.

signals.name: ARQOS
signals.description: A 4-bit identifier available to an implementation-defined system QoS policy.
values: Higher value recommended as higher priority
signals.verificationNote: Measure the configured arbitration/fairness policy; do not infer mandatory service from the numeric value alone.

signals.name: ARREGION
signals.description: Distinguishes up to 16 logical regions that can share an address range.
signals.verificationNote: Preserve the field through routing where the system uses region-based target behavior.

signals.name: ARUSER
signals.description: Optional application-defined information carried with the AR payload.
signals.verificationNote: If implemented, include ARUSER in stability, scoreboard context, and route preservation.

signals.name: ARVALID
signals.description: Asserted by the manager when the complete AR payload is valid.
signals.verificationNote: Must not depend on ARREADY and must remain asserted with stable payload until acceptance.

signals.name: ARREADY
signals.description: Asserted by the subordinate when it can accept the AR payload.
signals.verificationNote: Exercise independent AR stalls while other channels progress.

signals.name: RID
signals.description: Identifies the accepted AR transaction owning this R transfer.
signals.verificationNote: Keep RID stable through stalls and retire the per-ID entry only with accepted RLAST.

signals.name: RDATA
signals.description: Carries one read-data transfer for the transaction identified by RID.
signals.verificationNote: Select meaningful bytes from the predicted address/size and keep the complete payload stable during backpressure.

signals.name: RRESP
signals.description: Qualifies each R transfer independently; different beats in one burst can carry different responses.
signals.verificationNote: All declared R transfers still occur after an error; do not terminate the scoreboard entry early.

signals.name: RLAST
signals.description: Asserted with the final R transfer declared by ARLEN.
signals.verificationNote: Flag early, missing, or late RLAST and retire only when the final beat is accepted.

signals.name: RUSER
signals.description: Optional application-defined information returned per R transfer.
signals.verificationNote: Include RUSER in stability, beat attribution, and end-to-end checking when present.

signals.name: RVALID
signals.description: Asserted when RID, RDATA, RRESP, RLAST, and optional RUSER form a valid transfer.
signals.verificationNote: Must follow an accepted AR request, must not wait for RREADY, and must hold payload stable through stalls.

signals.name: RREADY
signals.description: Asserted by the manager when it can accept an R transfer.
signals.verificationNote: Randomize long and single-cycle stalls, especially on RLAST and error beats.
